title: Fulfilment Planning Reference: Lead Days, Slot Windows and Amendment Cutoffs
content:
Each fulfilment service of Northbeam Purchase Orders and Fulfilment sets its own planning figures. The least lead
days are the fewest days from the order to the earliest slot offered. The longest lead days are the days from the
order to the latest slot ordinarily offered. The windows offered are the slots the customer may choose from. The
amendment cutoff is the hours before the slot after which the order may no longer be amended.

| Fulfilment service | Least lead days | Longest lead days, ordinarily | Windows offered | Amendment cutoff, hours |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Standard Parcel Delivery | 2 | 7 | all day | 24 |
| Store Pickup Hold | 0 | 7 | store trading hours | 2 |
| Threshold Delivery | 3 | 14 | morning or afternoon | 48 |
| Room of Choice Delivery with Haul Away | 3 | 14 | morning or afternoon | 48 |
| White Glove Delivery and Installation | 5 | 21 | morning, afternoon or evening | 72 |
| Business Dock and Freight Delivery | 5 | 30 | business hours | 96 |

## The two ends of the lead figure (hypothetical days)

On Threshold Delivery, with its least lead of 3 days and its longest ordinary lead of 14 days: a slot two days after
the day of the order is earlier than the least lead days and is not among the slots offered; a slot three days after
is the earliest that is; a slot fourteen days after is the latest ordinarily offered.

Store Pickup Hold carries least lead days of 0, so the earliest slot it offers may fall on the day the order is
placed.

## Windows and cutoffs read across the services

The windows offered narrow or widen with the service: a single all-day slot on the parcel service, the store's own
trading hours on collection, morning or afternoon on the two two-person services, a third evening window on White
Glove Delivery and Installation, and business hours on the freight service. The amendment cutoff runs the other way,
from 2 hours on collection out to 96 hours on the freight service.
